mainTopic: A woman who discharges שכבת זרע (רואה or נוגעת?), and impurity from blood still inside the body
overview: This amud first finishes resolving a contradiction between רבא and רבי שמעון about a woman who discharges שכבת זרע after immersing. The גמרא rejects the idea that רבא was only worried some remained, because his wording is too certain. Instead it says both speak of a woman immersed in bed. רבא means one who turns over, so she will surely discharge, and רבי שמעון means one who lies still. רבא was really explaining the פסוק 'bathe in water and be impure until evening.' Next, רב שמואל בר ביסנא asks whether such a woman is a רואה (her own body produced the impurity) or a נוגעת (she only touched it). After two ways of explaining his question, אביי, רבא and רב יוסף all answer 'רואה.' אביי explains that רבי שמעון's 'דיה כבועלה' covers only impurity while the seed is still inside. A ברייתא then teaches that a נדה, זבה, שומרת יום כנגד יום and יולדת are impure even while the blood is still inside. The גמרא explains why יולדת is listed with רב's ruling about blood uprooted while she goes down to or comes up from the מקוה. רבי ירמיה objects that this blood is טומאה בלועה. רבי אבין compares it to נבלת עוף טהור in the throat, and רבי ירמיה asks whether the cases are really alike.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that רבא only worried some semen remained
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers saying that רבא was only worried that some שכבת זרע might remain. It rejects this, because then רבא would have said 'we are concerned' and not 'it is impossible.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to say that רבא only meant that perhaps some semen remained, then he should have said 'We are concerned that perhaps some remained!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible way out of the contradiction and then immediately knocks it down by looking at רבא's exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested answer was that רבא is only voicing a worry that some שכבת זרע stayed behind. But רבא said 'it is impossible for her not to discharge,' which is a statement of certainty, not a doubt. If he meant a doubt, he would have used the word חיישינן ('we are concerned'). So this answer does not fit his words.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a suggested answer, usually about to be rejected)
It remained; some was left over
We are concerned (language of doubt or worry, not certainty)
If so
He should have said (the wording would need to be different)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof here is entirely from wording. 'Impossible that she won't discharge' means certainty. 'We are concerned that perhaps' means doubt. רבא used the language of certainty, so a doubt-based answer can't be what he meant.

phrases.english: And if you would say: perhaps some remained,
phrases.notes: He means: perhaps she discharged most of the semen, and רבא was only worried that a little stayed inside.

phrases.english: if so,
he should have said: 'We are concerned that perhaps some remained'!
phrases.notes: In fact רבא said 'it is impossible for her not to discharge,' which sounds certain, not doubtful.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דִּילְמָא אִשְׁתְּיַיר — אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempt on the daf to reconcile רבא with רבי שמעון. It proposes a fix and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the answer that רבא only worried some שכבת זרע might remain.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא's wording ('impossible that she won't discharge') expresses certainty. A worry would have been phrased as 'חיישינן שמא נשתייר.'

steps.title: Both cases are about a woman immersed in bed: turning over versus lying still
steps.stepSummary: The new answer: both רבא and רבי שמעון speak of a woman who was immersed while still in bed. רבא means a woman who turns over in bed, so she will surely discharge. רבי שמעון means a woman who lies still, so she won't.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, according to רבא too, the case is where they immersed her in bed. And there is no contradiction: here (רבא) it is a woman who turns over, and there (רבי שמעון) it is a woman who does not turn over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer to the contradiction by splitting the cases. One case is a woman who moves around in bed, and the other is a woman who stays still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, the case of 'they immersed her in bed' was used only for רבי שמעון's ruling. Now the גמרא says רבא is also talking about that same setup. The difference is movement: a woman who turns from side to side will certainly discharge within three days, while one who lies still will not. So each ruling is correct for its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous approach and offers a new one)
They immersed her while she was in bed, so she did not get up and walk around
She turns over from side to side
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there (each ruling applies to a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction is solved by movement in bed. A woman who turns over will certainly discharge (רבא), and a woman who does not turn over will not (רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rava too,
it is where they immersed her in bed,
phrases.notes: Others did the immersion for her while she stayed in bed, so she never got up and walked around.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult:
here, where she turns over,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is רבא's statement.

phrases.english: there, where she does not turn over.
phrases.notes: 'There' is רבי שמעון's ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לְרָבָא נָמֵי, שֶׁהִטְבִּילוּהָ בַּמִּטָּה, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 1 with a new distinction between the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two rulings deal with different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא and רבי שמעון seem to disagree about whether a woman who had relations will discharge after immersion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both deal with a woman immersed in bed. If she turns over she will discharge (רבא). If she lies still she will not (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: רבא was explaining the פסוק of 'bathe in water and be impure until evening'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבא was commenting on a פסוק. The Torah says the woman is pure by evening, and רבא says that applies only when she doesn't turn over. If she does turn over, she may not eat תרומה for all three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא is commenting on a פסוק, and this is what he means: when the Torah wrote 'and they shall bathe in water and be impure until evening,' that is where she does not turn over. But where she does turn over, for all three days she is forbidden to eat תרומה, because it is impossible for her not to discharge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבא's statement comes from. He is explaining a פסוק and limiting it to a woman who does not turn over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא 15:18) implies that after relations, the woman immerses and is pure by evening. רבא says this is true only for a woman who does not turn over. A woman who turns over will surely discharge שכבת זרע during the three days, and each discharge makes her impure again, so she cannot eat תרומה that whole time.

keyTerms.meaning: He is standing on (commenting on) a פסוק
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
And they shall be impure until the evening
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which may only be eaten in purity
She will discharge (expel) the שכבת זרע

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah's 'pure by evening' applies to a woman who does not turn over. A woman who turns over may not eat תרומה for three days, since she is sure to discharge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבא is not arguing with the Torah's rule. He is defining the case the פסוק is talking about.

phrases.english: And Rava is standing on a verse,
phrases.notes: He means רבא was explaining a פסוק.

phrases.english: and this is what he is saying:
When the Merciful One wrote
'and they shall bathe in water and be impure until the evening,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:18

phrases.english: that is where she does not turn over;
but where she turns over,
for all three days
she is forbidden to eat teruma,
for it is impossible for her not to discharge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the turning-over distinction from step 2 and reads רבא's statement as an explanation of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading רבא's statement as a limit on the case a פסוק describes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's three-day rule might seem to conflict with the Torah's 'impure until the evening.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks of a woman who does not turn over. רבא adds that a woman who turns over may not eat תרומה for three days.

steps.title: Is a woman who discharges semen a 'רואה' or a 'נוגעת'?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר ביסנא asks אביי what kind of impurity a woman has when she discharges שכבת זרע. Is it like someone whose own body produced the impurity, or like someone who only touched it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר ביסנא asked אביי: a woman who discharges שכבת זרע, is she considered one who 'sees' or one who 'touches'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It asks how to classify the impurity of a woman who discharges שכבת זרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to view her. One is that she is like a רואה, someone whose own body produced the impurity, like a man who had an emission. The other is that she is only a נוגעת, someone who came into contact with שכבת זרע as it left her body. The question sets up a discussion of which category she belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who discharges
Semen
One who 'sees,' meaning her own body produced the impurity, like a בעל קרי
One who 'touches,' meaning she only came into contact with impurity

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בִּיסְנָא מֵאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Bisna asked Abaye:
a woman who discharges semen,
is she one who 'sees,'
phrases.notes: 'Sees' means her own body produced the impurity, like a man who had an emission.

phrases.english: or is she one who 'touches'?
phrases.notes: 'Touches' means she only had contact with something impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בִּיסְנָא מֵאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the רבא and רבי שמעון discussion to a new question about how to classify this woman's impurity.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a woman who discharges שכבת זרע impure as a רואה (her body produced the impurity) or as a נוגעת (she only touched it)?

steps.title: Three practical differences of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists what changes depending on whether she is a רואה or a נוגעת: breaking her count of clean days, becoming impure from any amount, and becoming impure while it is still inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference is whether it breaks her count, whether even a tiny amount makes her impure, and whether it makes her impure while still inside as if it had come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב שמואל בר ביסנא's question by explaining why it matters in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is a רואה, the discharge is like her own bodily impurity. It breaks a זבה's seven clean days, makes her impure in any amount, and makes her impure even before it leaves her body. If she is only a נוגעת, none of these apply: there is no break in the count, a minimum amount is needed, and she becomes impure only once it comes out.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that results
To break (cancel) a זבה's count of seven clean days
With any amount, even a tiny bit
Inside the body just as if it were outside

steps.whyThisMatters: These three differences show that the רואה/נוגעת question is not just a label. It changes real halachic outcomes.

phrases.english: The practical difference is whether it breaks her count,
phrases.notes: This is about a זבה counting seven clean days. If this counts as her own 'seeing,' it ruins the count.

phrases.english: whether it makes her impure in any amount,
and whether it makes her impure inside just as outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question from Step 4 by showing its practical results.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three outcomes apply: breaking the count, impurity from any amount, and impurity while still inside?

steps.title: Either way, the question seems already answered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question. If he knew the earlier teaching, it already answers him: רבנן say רואה and רבי שמעון says נוגעת. If he did not know it, logic says נוגעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem. If he heard the teaching, then according to the רבנן she is a רואה, and according to רבי שמעון she is a נוגעת. And if he did not hear it, it makes sense that she is a נוגעת!
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא attacks the question itself and says there seems to be nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching already showed that the רבנן make her impure even while the discharge is inside, which is the rule for a רואה. רבי שמעון makes her impure only once it comes out, which is the rule for a נוגעת. Without that teaching, plain logic says נוגעת, since the שכבת זרע did not come from her own body.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (a two-sided challenge)
A woman whose own body produced the impurity
A woman who only touched the impurity
It makes sense, it is logical

steps.confusionAlert: Here מַתְנִיתִין does not mean the משנה of this פרק. It refers to the earlier teaching where רבנן and רבי שמעון argue.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem!
If he heard the teaching,
phrases.notes: This is the earlier teaching where the רבנן and רבי שמעון argue about when she becomes impure.

phrases.english: then according to the Rabbis she is one who 'sees,'
and according to Rabbi Shimon she is one who 'touches.'
And if he did not hear the teaching,
it makes sense that she is one who 'touches'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question from Steps 4–5 is a real question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמואל בר ביסנא's question to אביי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possibilities leave the question with no room: the teaching answers it for each opinion, and without the teaching logic answers it.

steps.title: He was asking only according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: He did know the teaching. According to the רבנן the answer was clear to him. His question was only according to רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he heard the teaching. According to the רבנן he had no question. When he asks, it is according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the question to one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts that the רבנן clearly treat her as a רואה. But for רבי שמעון, the teaching only shows that she is not impure while it is inside. It does not settle the other differences, so there is still something to ask there. Step 14 gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (the earlier assumption stands)
According to the opinion of
He is asking, it is a question for him

steps.whatToRemember: The question 'רואה or נוגעת?' is asked only according to רבי שמעון, because for the רבנן she is clearly a רואה.

phrases.english: Really, he heard the teaching,
and according to the Rabbis he had no question;
when he asks,
it is according to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מה נפשך challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the question to one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching seemed to fully settle the question for both opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: It settles the question only for the רבנן. For רבי שמעון there is still a real question, which אביי answers in step 14.

steps.title: Which part of the question was really being asked
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון, the question is not about impurity while the seed is still inside. It is only about breaking the count and impurity from any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not ask whether the seed makes her impure while still inside, the same as outside. His question was only about breaking her count and becoming impure from any amount. What is the law there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows down exactly what רב שמואל בר ביסנא was asking according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 listed three differences between a רואה and a נוגעת. The third one, impurity while the seed is still inside, is already settled by רבי שמעון's own words. So only the first two are still open.

keyTerms.meaning: To break or cancel her count of clean days
In any amount, even a tiny bit
Inside the body the same as outside
He was not asking about this

phrases.english: And about making her impure while it is inside, the same as outside —
he was not asking about that,
phrases.notes: This is the third difference from step 5. רבי שמעון already said she is impure only once it comes out.

phrases.english: when he did ask,
it was about breaking her count and making her impure in any amount. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 7's answer by saying exactly which part of the question is still open according to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe all three differences were open according to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only breaking the count and impurity from any amount are in doubt.

steps.title: The two sides of the question according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי שמעון's 'it is enough for her to be like the man' only covers the inside-versus-outside issue, and for the other two she is a רואה. Or maybe it covers everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי שמעון says 'it is enough for her to be like the man who had relations with her,' maybe that only applies to impurity inside versus outside. For breaking the count and impurity from any amount, maybe she is a רואה. Or perhaps there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out both sides of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: רבי שמעון's leniency is narrow and covers only the inside/outside issue, so for the other two laws she is still a רואה. Side two: his reasoning makes her a נוגעת for everything.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for her to be like the man who had relations with her; she is not stricter than him
One whose own body produced the impurity
One who only touched the impurity
There is no difference

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, the question is whether his leniency covers only the inside/outside issue or all three laws.

phrases.english: When רבי שמעון says
'it is enough for her to be like the man who had relations with her,'
maybe that applies only to making her impure inside the same as outside,
but for breaking her count and making her impure in any amount,
she is a רואה,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two possible sides of the narrowed question from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון's 'דיה כבועלה' make her a נוגעת for all laws, or only for the inside/outside issue?

steps.title: Second version: he never heard the ברייתא, and his reason came from סיני
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רב שמואל בר ביסנא didn't know the ברייתא. He thought she might be a רואה because the Torah was strict with בעלי קריין at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he really had not heard the ברייתא. His question was this: since the Merciful One was strict at סיני with men who had a seminal emission, maybe she is a רואה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the challenge in step 6. It explains why someone who did not know the ברייתא could still think she is a רואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said that without the ברייתא, logic says נוגעת. This version answers that סיני shows this kind of impurity is especially strict. So treating her like a רואה is a real possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the ברייתא with the argument between רבנן and רבי שמעון
Men who had a seminal emission
The Merciful One; the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is a second way of answering the challenge from step 6: here he never knew the ברייתא at all.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
really, he had not heard the ברייתא,
and this is what he was asking:
since the Merciful One was strict
with men who had a seminal emission at סיני,
phrases.notes: שמות 19:15

phrases.english: she is a רואה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, לְעוֹלָם לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 6, instead of step 7's answer that he knew the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation of why he asked
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the ברייתא, logic clearly says נוגעת, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strictness at סיני gives a reason to think she is a רואה.

steps.title: Other side: סיני was a one-time rule
steps.stepSummary: Maybe we cannot learn from סיני, because it was a one-time rule. Proof: זבים and מצורעים are stricter, yet they were not kept away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps we do not learn from סיני, because it was a one-time special rule. After all, זבים and מצורעים are stricter, yet the Merciful One was not strict with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question in this second version: the rule at סיני may not teach us anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סיני were a real measure of how severe an impurity is, the stricter זבים and מצורעים would have been kept away too. They were not. So the rule at סיני was a one-time thing, and we cannot use it to make her a רואה.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn or derive from it
A special, unusual rule that we cannot learn other laws from
Men with a זיבה discharge, a severe impurity
People with צרעת

steps.whatToRemember: The second version of the question is whether the strictness at סיני teaches that seed is a 'רואה' type of impurity, or was just a one-time חידוש.

phrases.english: Or perhaps we do not learn from סיני,
because it was a special one-time rule,
since זבים and מצורעים, who are more severe,
and the Merciful One was not strict with them.
phrases.notes: He means they were not kept away from the giving of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא: לָא גָּמְרִינַן מִסִּינַי, דְּחִדּוּשׁ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question raised in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the strictness toward בעלי קריין at סיני teach us that a woman who discharges seed is a רואה, or was סיני a one-time rule?

steps.title: Three sages answer: she counts as a רואה
steps.stepSummary: אביי, then רבא, then רב יוסף each answer רב שמואל בר ביסנא the same way: the woman counts as a רואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: She is a רואה. He went and asked רבא, who said: She is a רואה. He came to רב יוסף, who said: She is a רואה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the answer to רב שמואל בר ביסנא's question from step 9. He asks three great sages, and all three say the same thing: she is treated like a רואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The short answer 'she is a רואה' means that for at least some laws she is treated like someone who had an emission herself. In the first version of the question (steps 7-9), that means רבי שמעון's leniency does not cover everything. The answer is so short that it does not yet say which laws, and that sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who 'sees', meaning someone who has an emission herself
She is
He asked him
He came before him

phrases.english: He said to him: She is one who saw.
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering. 'One who saw' means she counts like someone who had the emission herself.

phrases.english: He came and asked רבא,
he said to him: She is one who saw.
He came before רב יוסף,
he said to him: She is one who saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question in step 9, after the side discussion in steps 10-11, and gives the answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון's 'it is enough for her to be like the man' cover all three issues, or only inside-versus-outside?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She counts as a רואה. Three separate sages give this same answer.

steps.title: You all spit the same saliva
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר ביסנא goes back to אביי and complains that all three gave the same unhelpful answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came back to אביי and said to him: You all spit the same saliva.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר ביסנא is not satisfied. He goes back to אביי and tells him that all three sages just repeated the same short answer without explaining it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His complaint is that 'she is a רואה' does not seem to fit רבי שמעון, who said 'it is enough for her to be like the man'. If she is like the man, how can she also be a רואה? He wants to know how the two fit together, and this sets up אביי's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back, returned
Saliva, spit
You (plural) spit out

phrases.english: He came back before אביי,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כּוּלְּכוּ בְּרוּקָּא חֲדָא תָּפִיתוּ.
phrases.english: he said to him: You all spit with one saliva.
phrases.notes: A saying: you're all repeating the same thing without adding any explanation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer 'she is a רואה' given by all three sages.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer seems to clash with רבי שמעון's 'it is enough for her to be like the man', and no one explained how it fits.

steps.title: אביי explains: 'like the man' only covers inside versus outside
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רבי שמעון's leniency only applies to impurity while the seed is inside. For breaking the count and impurity from any amount, she is a רואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: I told you correctly. רבי שמעון only said 'it is enough for her to be like the man' about being impure inside as outside. But for breaking the count and being impure from any amount, she is a רואה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his answer and explains its limits. רבי שמעון's 'like the man' rule covers only one of the three issues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three issues: (1) impurity while the seed is still inside, (2) breaking a זבה's count of seven clean days, and (3) impurity from any small amount. רבי שמעון compared her to the man only for issue 1, so she is not impure until it comes out. For issues 2 and 3 she is a רואה, so even a tiny amount makes her impure and breaks her count.

keyTerms.meaning: Well, correctly
He only said it up to this point; his ruling goes no further
It is enough for her to be like the man who was with her
Inside the body just as outside it
To break, here meaning to cancel her count of clean days
From any amount at all

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי שמעון's 'it is enough for her to be like the man' covers only impurity while the seed is still inside. For breaking her count and for impurity from any amount, she is a רואה.
steps.confusionAlert: Being 'like the man' and being a 'רואה' are not opposites here. Each one applies to different laws.

phrases.english: He said to him: I told you well,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: רבי שמעון only said
'it is enough for her to be like the man who was with her'
only about being impure inside as outside,
but about breaking the count and being impure from any amount —
she is one who saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the complaint in step 13 by explaining how far the short answer reaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: רבי שמעון's rule covers only one issue.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'It is enough for her to be like the man' covers all the laws, so she could not be a רואה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only inside-versus-outside. For breaking the count and impurity from any amount, she is a רואה.

steps.title: ברייתא: women impure from blood still inside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a נדה, a זבה, a שומרת יום כנגד יום and a יולדת are all impure even while the blood is still inside the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A נדה, a זבה, a woman who keeps a day for a day, and a יולדת all become impure inside as outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, a ברייתא about blood that has not yet left the body. It lists four kinds of women who become impure even before the blood comes out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of what רבי שמעון said about semen in the last step. With blood, these women are impure as soon as the blood leaves its source, even if it is still inside. The list of four sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman during her monthly period
A woman who sees blood outside her regular days
A woman who must wait one clean day for a day she saw blood
A woman after childbirth

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A menstruating woman, and a zavah,
and one who keeps a day for a day, and a woman after childbirth —
all of them become impure inside as outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about impurity from blood still inside the body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה, a זבה, a שומרת יום כנגד יום and a יולדת are impure while the blood is still inside, just as after it comes out.

steps.title: Why list יולדת separately?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא mentions a יולדת, since her blood already counts as נדה blood or זבה blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other cases make sense. But a יולדת: if it is during her נדה days, she is a נדה, and if it is during her זיבה days, she is a זבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's list. Listing יולדת seems unnecessary, because she already fits into one of the earlier categories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any blood a יולדת sees comes either in her נדה days or in her זיבה days. Either way, she is already covered by 'נדה' or 'זבה' in the list. So the extra word 'יולדת' seems to add nothing, and the גמרא wants to know why it is there.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense
Fine, it works (literally 'to life')
The days of the month when blood counts as נדה blood
The days of the month when blood counts as זיבה blood

phrases.english: Granted, all of them, fine,
but a woman after childbirth:
if in the days of niddah, she is a niddah,
if in the days of zivah, she is a zavah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions one item in the ברייתא's list from step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every case of a יולדת already falls under נדה or זבה, so listing her separately seems pointless.

steps.title: The case is a woman going to immerse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed to mention a יולדת for the case where she goes down to the מקוה to move from impurity to purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where she went down to immerse, to go from impurity to purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16. It says the ברייתא mentions a יולדת for one specific case: the moment she goes down to the מקוה at the end of her impure days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a יולדת's blood just counts as נדה blood or זבה blood, so listing her looks extra. But at the moment she immerses, she is switching from impure days to pure days. The ברייתא teaches us something new about blood that is uprooted right at that switching point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... (a specific case that makes the teaching necessary)
She went down to immerse in a מקוה
From impurity to purity

phrases.english: No, it is needed where she went down to immerse
phrases.notes: This is the time after her impure days after birth are over (seven days for a boy, fourteen for a girl).

phrases.english: from impurity to purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 about why a יולדת is listed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the teaching to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning a יולדת seems extra, since her blood is already נדה or זבה blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is teaching the special case of a יולדת going down to immerse to move from impurity to purity.

steps.title: רב's ruling on blood uprooted during immersion
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if blood is uprooted while the יולדת goes down to the מקוה, she is impure; if on the way up, she is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי זירא said in the name of רבי חייא בר אשי in the name of רב: A יולדת who went down to immerse to go from impurity to purity, and blood was uprooted from her: if on the way down, she is impure; if on the way up, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רב that fits the case it just described. It shows the exact law for a יולדת whose blood is uprooted while she is immersing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood was uprooted but did not leave her body. On the way down she is still in her impure days, so the blood inside makes her impure. On the way up she has already immersed and her pure days have started, so the blood does not make her impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood was uprooted (came loose from the womb) but did not yet come out
Going down (into the מקוה)
Coming up (out of the מקוה)
A woman after childbirth

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the practical example of the ברייתא's rule that a יולדת is impure even while the blood is still inside.

phrases.english: And this is like what Rabbi Zeira said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
A woman after childbirth who went down to immerse
from impurity to purity,
and blood was uprooted from her
phrases.notes: It came loose inside her but did not come out of her body.

phrases.english: on the way down, she is impure,
on the way up, she is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and fills in the case given in step 17 with an actual ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood uprooted inside a יולדת on her way down to immerse makes her impure; on her way up, she is pure.

steps.title: Why is swallowed blood impure?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks why she is impure on the way down, since the blood is still hidden inside her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: On the way down, why is she impure? It is swallowed impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges the first half of רב's ruling. He points out that the blood is still inside her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that impurity hidden inside a body (טומאה בלועה) does not make things impure. Since the blood never came out, it should be 'swallowed' and not make her impure. So why does רב say she is impure on the way down?

keyTerms.meaning: Swallowed impurity: something impure that is hidden inside a body, which normally does not make things impure
Why?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not arguing that a יולדת's blood is not impure. He is asking only about blood that is still stuck inside her body.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
On the way down, why is she impure?
It is swallowed impurity!
phrases.notes: He means the blood is still inside her body, and hidden impurity usually doesn't make anything impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first half of רב's ruling from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that blood uprooted on the way down makes her impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood still inside the body is טומאה בלועה, which normally does not make things impure.

steps.title: רבי זירא sends him to רבי אבין
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רבי ירמיה to go ask רבי אבין, who agreed to רבי זירא's explanation in the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go ask רבי אבין, because I explained it to him, and he nodded his head to me in the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא does not answer directly. He sends רבי ירמיה to רבי אבין, setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא says he already explained the reason to רבי אבין, and רבי אבין nodded in agreement. This shows the explanation was accepted, and that רבי אבין can repeat it.

keyTerms.meaning: Go ask him
He nodded with his head (in agreement)
The study hall

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל שַׁיְילֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אָבִין,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go ask Rabbi Avin,
because I explained it to him,
and he nodded his head to me
in the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי ירמיה's challenge by sending him to someone who heard and agreed to the answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct answer yet; רבי ירמיה is told to ask רבי אבין, who accepted רבי זירא's explanation.

steps.title: Compared to נבלת עוף טהור
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין answers that the חכמים treated this blood like נבלת עוף טהור, which makes clothes impure while still in the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and asked him. He said to him: They made it like נבלת עוף טהור, which makes clothes impure while it is in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה goes to רבי אבין, who gives the answer to the challenge of step 19. He compares the blood to a case where swallowed impurity still makes things impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבלת עוף טהור makes the clothes of the person eating it impure while it is in his throat, even though it is already swallowed. So swallowed impurity can sometimes still count. The חכמים treated the יולדת's uprooted blood the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher bird that died without proper שחיטה
The throat (the place of swallowing)
They (the חכמים) made it / treated it as

phrases.english: He went and asked him; he said to him:
They made it like the carcass of a kosher bird
which makes clothes impure
phrases.notes: He means the clothes of the person who is eating it.

phrases.english: while it is in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer that step 20 promised.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Swallowed impurity never makes anything impure, so the blood inside should not make her impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like נבלת עוף טהור in the throat, this swallowed blood was treated as making her impure.

steps.title: Are the two cases really alike?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the case of the bird is really similar to the case of the יולדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes back on רבי אבין's comparison. He asks if the bird case and the יולדת case are really the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer built on a comparison only works if the two cases match. By asking 'מי דמי', רבי ירמיה is saying the cases may be different, so the comparison may not prove anything. The גמרא will explain the difference next.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it similar? (a challenge saying the two cases are different)

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
phrases.notes: רבי ירמיה is asking רבי אבין whether the bird case really matches the יולדת case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבין's comparison to נבלת עוף טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison only proves something if the two cases are truly alike, and these may not be.
